text: AppShell: the window every studio app shares. What: one owned window with a resizable splitter, a tab per task, an optional embedded preview (TGlyph on the right, or TMetrics on top) and a status line. The shell owns the content-driven initial window size and title; embedded widgets never size or title themselves. Later user resizing is retained. Edits: host-mode tab writes go through AppShell.history(label, glyphs, ...) . It first calls core.edit_guards.require_history_scope and then the existing core.history commit path, so every write is one named Undo step on the explicit live layers the caller passes. A refusal or a partial write never raises out of a button: its message goes to the status line. Use: shell = show_app("Kerning Studio", preview="tmetrics", tabs=[TabSpec(...)]) . A tab spec is any object with title and build(shell) ; build returns an Owned (closed with the shell) or a plain widget.

text: Run FontLab's PostScript autohinter on the selected glyphs, in one or all masters. What it does: For each selected glyph and chosen master, the script runs FontLab's own autohinter on the layer. It works from the font's hinting settings (alignment zones and standard stems). The table shows the horizontal and vertical hint counts before and after. FontLab's source does not touch TrueType instructions here. How it works: A non-modal panel lists every glyph and master with its hint counts, or the reason why the layer is skipped. Apply reads the font again and calls the native flLayer.autohint() on every planned layer, all in one Undo step through the shared module fly.ap.core.history.glyphs. Read-back reports a layer that has an outline but no PostScript hints after the call. The hint counts and the panel are shared (fly.ap.hints.postscript, fly.ap.contours.selection.panel.model). Native call caveat: FontLab's source shows that autohint switches the package master temporarily, writes hinting options and stored hinting data, and can attach hints as node links. These effects extend beyond the notified layers; the script does not check them. TrueType instructions are separate. Why this design: - The hints come from FontLab's own autohinter, not from a script algorithm. - The script adds what the menu command does not: every master in one step, a count of hints before and after, and one Undo step. - Automatic layers and glyphs with automatic layers are never edited. A base of automatic composites is skipped unless you tick "Edit bases of auto glyphs anyway": the change notification makes FontLab rebuild those composites, which can drop their anchors and locks, and Undo does not restore them. Locked layers and layers without contours are skipped. - Apply discloses queued ids and their possible date changes. The script does not call UpdateAll (fl#8537). How to use: Set the alignment zones and standard stems in Font Info first. Select glyphs in the Font window. Run the script. Choose the current master or all masters, check the table and press Autohint. Each Apply is recorded as one Undo step. Benefit: A whole selection gets fresh PostScript hints in every master, with the counts in view, in one step. Credit: Adapted from the author's own FontLab sample, Apache-2.0 (hints_autohint.py, "Autohint Selected Layers").

text: Remove PostScript stem hints from the selected glyphs, horizontal and/or vertical. What it does: For each selected glyph and chosen master, the script removes the horizontal hints, the vertical hints or both from the layer. FontLab's source does not touch plain guidelines or TrueType instructions here. The table shows the hint counts before and after. How it works: A non-modal panel lists every glyph and master with its hint counts, or the reason why the layer is skipped. A layer without hints in the chosen directions is listed and skipped. Apply reads the font again and calls the native flLayer.removeHints(horizontal, vertical) on every planned layer, all in one Undo step through the shared module fly.ap.core.history.glyphs. After the write it counts the hints again and reports any layer that still has hints in a chosen direction. The hint counts and the panel are shared (fly.ap.hints.postscript, fly.ap.contours.selection.panel.model). Why this design: - The removal is FontLab's own call, so hints are removed exactly as the menu command removes them. - The script adds what the menu command does not: every master in one step, one direction only, the counts in view and one Undo step. - Automatic layers and glyphs with automatic layers are never edited. A base of automatic composites is skipped unless you tick "Edit bases of auto glyphs anyway": the change notification makes FontLab rebuild those composites, which can drop their anchors and locks, and Undo does not restore them. Locked layers are skipped. - Apply discloses queued ids and their possible date changes. The script does not call UpdateAll (fl#8537). How to use: Select glyphs in the Font window. Run the script. Tick the directions, choose the current master or all masters, check the table and press Remove Hints. Each Apply is recorded as one Undo step. Benefit: Clean hint-free layers before a new autohint pass or a TrueType-only export, in every master, in one step. Credit: Adapted from the author's own FontLab sample, Apache-2.0 (hints_remove.py, "Remove PostScript Hints").

text: Echo suppression for windows that write to the font they follow. What: Echo remembers the fingerprint a window produced after its own successful write. When the follow callback later fires, Echo.stale(current) says whether the window must refresh: False only while the font still matches that recorded fingerprint, so the window's own write does not reset it. Any other fingerprint is an external change: the token is dropped and every later call refreshes until the next own write records a new token. Use: fontlabapp.fontui.tmetrics records after each LSB/RSB/width/kerning write and checks in its follow callback. Why: Qt-free so the rule is unit-tested without FontLab; fingerprints come from fontlabapp.fontui.tmetrics_model.fingerprint .

text: Align contour start nodes and directions to the first declared master. What: Align contour start nodes and directions to the first declared master. How: Compare normalized point geometry among cyclic point-type matches in both directions. Choose the unique closest order; keep a glyph when scores tie. Read back the actual point coordinates, start and winding after each write. Why: Repair master point ordering before interpolation. Use: Choose All masters, inspect the start and direction changes, then Apply. Benefit: Adds a batch preview to start-node and direction commands. The non-modal panel previews the selected glyphs and chosen masters. A glyph with shared, scaled or rotated outline shapes is kept as a whole. Automatic-layer owners are kept. Bases of automatic composites are kept unless the shared consent option is enabled. Each Apply is recorded as one Undo step through the App history writer. Reload after changing the selection. Independent behaviour rewrite after Simon Cozens, GlyphsScripts/Superaligner.py, MIT, copyright 2017 Simon Cozens. Repository: https://github.com/simoncozens/GlyphsScripts . text: TGlyph: a single-glyph view that follows FontLab. What: one glyph of a font on an explicit layer (the layer selector lists the font's layers/masters and starts on the default layer). The glyph name field completes existing names; Prev/Next step through the glyph order. The canvas draws the filled outline, on-curve points (squares; circles when smooth) and off-curve points (small circles) with handle lines, a start point marker, components (drawn, not editable), named anchors, the baseline, the advance box and the vertical metric lines. Zoom with the wheel, + / - or Fit ( 0 ); pan with space-drag or a middle-button drag; click a point to select it (Shift adds or removes) or drag a rubber band. Editing: drag selected points (the handles of a moved on-curve point follow), nudge with the arrows (Shift: 10 units), Delete removes points, and the pen tool ( P ; V returns to select) adds line points to a new open contour, closes it on its first point and ends with Escape. Each gesture writes once, on release or on the key, through fontlabapp.fontui.tglyph_edit.Editor to the shown layer only; a drag only previews until release, and a failed write reverts with its reason in the status line. FontLab edits and Undo/Redo refresh within the follow delay, keeping zoom, pan and selection while the point structure stays the same. "Follow FontLab current glyph" switches to the glyph FontLab shows when it changes (names absent from this font are ignored). Refreshes go through fontlabapp.fontui.livesync.Echo so the window's own writes can be skipped. Use: show_tglyph() for FontLab's current font and glyph, or TGlyph(font, name, layer) over any FontParts-style font. Why: geometry, hit-testing and change detection live in the Qt-free fontlabapp.fontui.tglyph_model and the edits in tglyph_edit ; this module only draws and forwards input.

text: Qt-free point edits for TGlyph: move, delete, rubber band and redraw. What: pure functions over fontlabapp.fontui.tglyph_model values. move_points shifts the selected points; a moved on-curve point carries its adjacent off-curve handles (wrapping round a closed contour, not an open one). delete_points removes the selected points, and the handles of selected on-curve points, then normalise keeps each touched contour valid: a contour with no on-curve point left is dropped, handles left in front of a line or move point are dropped, a curve left without handles becomes a line, a cubic curve left with exactly one handle becomes a line (the lone handle is dropped rather than reinterpreted as an implied quadratic), a closed contour starts on an on-curve point and an open contour starts with a move point. points_in_rect is the rubber-band hit test in screen pixels and draw_contours replays contours into a point pen. Every coordinate is stored as a float so a written glyph fingerprints exactly like the same glyph read back. Editor is the gesture state over a TGlyphModel : select, toggle, rubber band, drag with a preview, nudge, delete and the pen tool. The pen's first click only sets Editor.pending (drawn as a preview, never written); the second click writes a two-point open contour, and Escape or a tool switch discards the pending point. Each gesture yields at most one Edit ; Editor.commit writes it once through font.edit_glyph(name, layer=..., undo_name="TGlyph: <action> <name>") , redrawing only the staged contours (components and anchors stay), and returns the fingerprint of the state it drew for fontlabapp.fontui.livesync.Echo . A failed write restores the pre-gesture glyph and re-raises. Use: fontlabapp.fontui.tglyph.TGlyph forwards canvas input to Editor . Why: the structural rules stay unit-testable without Qt or FontLab.
title: fontlabapp.fontui.tglyph_edit

text: Qt-free model behind the TGlyph window: one glyph on one explicit layer. What: read_glyph(font, name, layer) reads a glyph's contours, components, anchors and advance from font.getLayer(layer) through a point pen and returns plain values (never live glyph objects, which a FontLab commit invalidates). Components are decomposed through the same layer for drawing only; a missing base or a component cycle marks that component unavailable. When Fontport refuses the glyph itself ( UnsupportedCapability while loading its component graph), own_glyph reads the own contours from an aborted edit_glyph staging block, which writes nothing. View maps font units to screen pixels (y up in the font, y down on the screen) with zoom about a point, pan and fit. hit_point finds the point under the cursor within a tolerance in screen pixels. signature describes the point structure (contour count, point types, components) without coordinates, so a live follow can keep the selection while points only move; fingerprint digests every value a refresh shows, for fontlabapp.fontui.livesync.Echo . Use: TGlyphModel(font, name, layer) ; fontlabapp.fontui.tglyph draws it. Why: geometry, hit-testing and change detection stay testable without Qt.
title: fontlabapp.fontui.tglyph_model

text: TMetrics: a shaping, metrics and kerning window that follows and edits FontLab. What: type text (or /names ), features, direction, script and language; the canvas shows the shaped rows with the baseline and vertical metric lines, glyph boxes, sidebearing marks, kerning offsets and the selected glyph. The readout names the selected glyph's advance, LSB and RSB and the kerning pair before it (group or glyph pair). Click or press the arrow keys to select; double-click calls on_open_glyph(name) . The LSB, RSB, Width and Kerning fields write the selected glyph and the pair before it back to the font (press Return); Alt+Left/Right nudge the RSB and Ctrl+Alt+Left/Right the pair kerning (on macOS either Control or Command with Option; see HELP_TEXT ). A write to a group pair names the actual group keys in the status line. Each glyph write is one font.edit_glyph on the default layer named TMetrics: <LSB|RSB|width> <glyph> ; each kerning write is one font.kerning.apply named TMetrics: kerning <left> <right> , read back. FontLab edits (outlines, metrics, kerning, features) and Undo/Redo re-shape within the follow delay, keeping the text, the selection and the scroll position; the window's own writes are recognised by fontlabapp.fontui.livesync.Echo and do not reset it a second time. Use: show_tmetrics() over the current FontLab font (double-click opens fontlabapp.fontui.tglyph on that glyph, reusing one TGlyph window), or TMetrics(font, parent, on_open_glyph) over any FontParts-style font. Why: all layout and readout rules live in the Qt-free fontlabapp.fontui.tmetrics_model ; this module only draws and forwards input.

text: Explicit sources and destination folder; one run at a time. Start validates every job in FontLab first (Fontport's run() is eager) and writes nothing on failure. The work then runs in a separate Python 3.11+ with fontlab-fontport (python=..., else $FONTLABAPP_BATCH_PYTHON), so it never holds FontLab's GIL; each 50 ms poll reads at most 64 KiB and records at most 64 rows from a non-blocking socket on Darwin or pipe elsewhere. Output that is not a result row stops the run visibly. Cancel stops before the next font. Close (including parent or own-widget destruction) normally hands off cleanup without waiting; at the pending-child cap, overflow cleanup can wait up to KILL_WAIT (1.0 second) for the child after killing it. batch_worker.supervise watches for exit (termination after GRACE_SECONDS, killing later; a terminated font can leave a partial destination), then attempts scratch cleanup and schedules deletion of the surviving hidden, detached panel. Outputs are named -transformed.ufo and never replace a file.
title: fontlabapp.fontui.batch.BatchPanel

text: What: Add explicit Unicode values to selected glyphs in the current font. How: Paste a JSON object of glyph names and code points. Integers are decimal; strings are hexadecimal, with optional U+ or 0x prefix. A value can be a list. Existing codes stay in place. Why: Font > Generate Unicodes derives values from names. This map also encodes custom names and assigns several explicit values to one glyph. Usage: Select glyphs in the Font window and close Glyph editors. Paste a map, inspect the live table, then Apply Map. Use Selection reloads the glyph scope. Each Apply is recorded as one Undo step. Auto-layer owners, bases of automatic composites, unknown names and conflicting codes remain as named kept rows. Benefit: Apply a reusable character map without renaming outlines. Example: {"A": "0041", "space": [32, "00A0"]}. Repeated JSON keys and invalid Unicode scalars are refused. Several map rows cannot claim the same code. Only selected glyphs can change. Typing uses a detached font snapshot. Use Selection reloads it. Apply scans the font once and compares with the displayed preview; native read-back checks every changed list. A partial write directs you to Edit > Undo. JSON is pasted; NAM files and font-library maps are not loaded. Setup: FontLab 9, Python 3.11, Fly and App>=0.2.150.dev0. Modeless panel. Independent behaviour rewrite of TR-EncodeGlyphs.py by Vassil Kateliev, kateliev/TypeRig, MPL-2.0. https://github.com/kateliev/TypeRig No TypeRig code, private identifiers, comments or resources are copied.

text: What: Create a monthly numeral proof for the current font. How: Read Unicode assignments. Build a Monday-first calendar and report missing ASCII digits and the space separator. The HTML preview uses a reference font. Why: Glyph names do not identify Unicode coverage reliably. Usage: Set year and month. Select Build, then Copy. text: What: Save a review state and note in the current font's native glyph notes. How: Map an Unset/Todo/Review/Done combo and a literal note field to one table row with QDataWidgetMapper. Apply submits only that row, checks the captured glyph id and original note, then commits metadata through App history.commit. Why: Native notes travel with the font; existing free-form notes stay intact until the user explicitly applies a review state. Auto-layer glyphs are refused. Usage: Choose a row, select its state, enter a note and click Apply. Apply or Discard Changes before switching rows or closing. Each Apply is one Undo step. Benefit: Keep review decisions with the glyphs rather than in a separate draft. Requires: FontLab 9, Python 3.11, Fly and App names_edit, history, draft_signals and qt_properties. Native read-back failures show the Edit > Undo recovery. Independent rewrite of the Qt simplewidgetmapper and combowidgetmapper example idea. Based on the author's own FontLab sample, Apache-2.0. text: What: Keep a resumable zero-to-five-star review queue for the current font. How: A painted five-star delegate sets scores by click and edits existing items. Export JSON retains the full queue; Import reloads it after checking glyph names, score ranges, star consistency, duplicate keys and characters that PythonQt can replace. Why: A portable queue can be resumed without modifying native glyph metadata. Usage: Open a font and Refresh. Click within a star cell to set its score; Delete clears it. Export New before closing. To resume, Refresh the matching font and Import an exported queue. Import accepts UTF-8 BOM and normalizes CRLF or CR to LF. Benefit: Carry a review across sessions and reject incompatible queues clearly. Requires: FontLab 9, Python 3.11, Fly and App glyph_catalog, draft_signals and qt_properties. Invalid imports keep the visible queue and current scores. Independent rewrite of the Qt stardelegate example idea. Based on the author's own FontLab sample, Apache-2.0. text: What: Generate current-font glyph pairs from two explicit name lists. How: Combine all left/right names, or zip equal-length lists. Apply each side's suffix, then validate every resulting name against the current font. Why: Cartesian combinations expose spacing relationships absent from an adjacent-pair proof. Unencoded alternates remain usable through slash names. Usage: Enter space-separated names without slashes. Choose Product or Zip. Optional fillers are name lists. Copy Fresh Result to a Glyph window text bar. Benefit: Prepare every requested pair in stable order without editing kerning. This tool generates proofs. Use File > Export > Metrics for AFM kerning output and scriptmix Kerning > Classes Browser for class inspection. scriptmix Kerning > Missing Pairs also builds Cartesian combinations, filtered to missing kerning. This tool keeps all pairs and adds Zip, suffixes and fillers. It does not extract existing-kerning proof strings or export KRN, Unicode strings or OpenType class declarations. Independent behaviour-only rewrite of the pair-generation idea from Pairs.py. Credit: Vassil Kateliev and Karandash Type Foundry; kateliev/TypeRig, MPL-2.0. No TypeRig code, comments, icons or resources are included. Setup: FontLab 9, Python 3.11, Fly and App>=0.2.150.dev0.

text: Check proof text against current-font Unicode assignments. Setup: Use FontLab 9 with Python 3.11, Fly and fontlabapp. Click Enter Proof Text to open a modeless standard input dialog. text: Keep a reusable proof sample and check it against the current font. What: Save one proof string in an isolated example settings namespace. How: QSettings stores only proof/sample. Check Coverage reads the full current font catalogue with a glyph-count-scaled scan deadline capped at 120 seconds and a Scanning label. It reports covered and missing Unicode scalars as JSON. Why: Persist a personal proof across launches and fonts in this tool's own settings namespace. Coverage and clipboard output make that saved proof useful. Usage: Edit the sample, Save Sample, Check Coverage, or Copy Proof Text to paste in FontLab. Reset Saved Sample removes only this tool's key. Unsaved typing is not persisted; Save Sample is explicit. Coverage always captures the font again. Benefit: Keep a stable personal proof and compare encoding coverage across fonts. No font or selection changes occur. Unicode coverage is not shaping coverage. NUL and input-method transfer have known loss (fl#8567, fl#8568). This example also conservatively refuses NBSP, U+2028/U+2029 and lone surrogates; it requires exact proof text. This is a transfer policy, not a Unicode coverage limitation. Setup: FontLab 9, Python 3.11, Fly, App glyph_catalog and draft_signals. Independent rewrite of sandbox-settings. Based on the author's own FontLab sample, Apache-2.0. No original source body is redistributed.

text: What: Find unencoded glyphs and glyphs that share a Unicode in the current font. How: Read the public glyph catalogue. Count owners of each Unicode scalar, then filter and page only the issue rows. Double-click uses App scripting.select_glyphs; its Font-window guard refuses a Glyph window or a changed current font (fl#8528). Why: Keep an actionable Unicode checklist beside the Font window. Usage: Activate the Font window, run this script, and double-click an issue row. Type a name, issue or U+ value to filter. Refresh reads the current font again. If the status line asks for the Font window, click it and double-click the row again. The default dock area is right. show(..., area="left") chooses the left area; top and bottom are also valid. Drag the dock title to float it or dock it again. App widgets.create_panel floats the registered dock automatically when FontLab's macOS multi-window profile hides MainWindow. No separate main window is created. Close or the dock X calls handle.close_owned(): disconnect callbacks first, then OwnedWidget.close() removes the dock and schedules its widget for deletion. Benefit: Select the exact glyph that needs an encoding decision, without changing its Unicode values or geometry. Counts cover every issue, even on other pages. Setup: FontLab 9, Python 3.11, Fly and App with widgets, scripting, glyph_catalog, draft_signals and qt_properties. Independent rewrite of the Qt dockwidgets, menus, separations, basiclayouts and borderlayout example ideas (Qt/Nokia, Riverbank). Based on the author's own FontLab sample, Apache-2.0. No upstream code or assets copied. Native object ids guard the UI binding; fgId identifies the fontpr font. Raise ValueError when the bound font is no longer the active font.
title: fontlabapp.fontui.feature_blocks.read_feature_blocks

text: write_feature_blocks ( package : Any , expected : dict , updated : dict , * , references : Iterable [ str ], undo_name : str ) -> dict [ str , int ] Apply an exact source-bound feature plan with Fontport's history checks. All referenced glyphs and the complete source snapshot must still match. Fontport validates split-back, language synthesis and empty history slots before mutation, and notifies only package/features. Groups are untouched. Unexpected native errors may leave partial changes; they are not hidden. Refuse with ValueError when the font is inactive, the source differs from expected , or a referenced glyph is gone. Return {"changed": 0} when expected == updated and {"changed": 1} after a write. Feature codes missing a final newline, or with trailing spaces/tabs after it, are normalised by _terminated before comparing and staging. The master that was active before the write is restored in finally .

Return the applied values, or None when the staged kerning equals the current kerning (nothing is written). Raise TypeError for a model without kerning.apply and RuntimeError when the backend reads back different values. Shared by KerningEditor.edit and fontlabapp.fontui.tmetrics . Fontport writes kerning to the default master only (its set_kerning has no master argument). master names the master the caller resolved; when it is not the default master ( font.defaultLayerName ) the write is refused with ValueError before anything changes. None keeps the old behaviour: the default kerning target.

text: follow_changes ( owner , callback , fonts , delay_ms = CHANGE_DELAY_MS ) Call callback after FontLab reports changes; return signals connected. Connected whenever FontLab is present (nothing outside it); fonts() is read at each signal, so an owner whose fonts appear later starts following then. Signals count only while fonts() holds a FontLab-backed font, and glyph(s)Updated only for those documents. The first signal arms a single-shot timer that later signals never restart, so callback runs at most delay_ms after the first change even under a steady stream. Signals emitted while any follower's callback runs (refresh reads or writes, also from other open controls) are ignored, no callback is re-entered, and a timer that fires during another follower's callback runs after it. Before it, each FontLab-backed (Fontport) font is refreshed, which drops its loaded glyph and layer handles. owner.close() disconnects everything; a pending timer then fires into nothing.
title: fontlabapp.fontui.lifecycle.follow_changes

text: follow_history ( owner , callback ) Call callback after FontLab's Undo/Redo actions; return connections made. FontLab connects its own handlers first, so ours run after the history step. Outside FontLab (no fontlab module) nothing is connected. owner.close() disconnects these like every other owned connection.
title: fontlabapp.fontui.lifecycle.follow_history

text: Follow selected nodes as you edit; inspect coordinates, offsets and distances. What it does: Open a glyph, run this script and select nodes. Both tables update every 400 ms. Copy exports the displayed node coordinates as tab-separated lines. Contour numbers start at one; node indices start at zero. Component contours are excluded. The modeless panel reads the bound font only. Switching or closing that font stops polling; reopen the tool to bind another font. No font data is written. How it works: Read selected own nodes on the bound glyph layer and publish both tables from the same snapshot. Poll every 400 ms and recheck that snapshot before Copy. Why this design: Live coordinates support measurement while a stale-font refusal prevents copying values from a different document under the old panel title. How to use: Open a glyph and run Contours > Node Coordinates Panel. Select nodes, inspect positions and distances, then use Copy for the displayed tab- separated coordinates. Benefit: Measure selected nodes without moving them; Close stops polling and releases owned connections.

text: Insert coincident nodes, with optional coincident cubic handles. What: Duplicate selected on-curve nodes in selected editor layers or masters. How: Read node indices from each glyph's selected reference layer. Require the same contour closure and node types in every target master, then insert backwards. The optional two handles create a zero-length cubic instead of a line. Why: One selection controls corresponding nodes across masters. Unrelated glyphs never inherit indices from the first glyph. The table previews counts. Use: Select nodes, open this panel, choose scope and handles, then Duplicate. Reload selection after changing glyphs. Disable Keep masters compatible only when you intend to edit the current master separately. Benefit: Prepare matching contour construction without dragging new nodes. Locked, shared, transformed, quadratic and automatic outlines are kept and listed. Other glyphs in the selection can still be edited. Master scope targets only master layers. Only selected editor layers also supports manual auxiliary layers and intentionally changes their structure without a cross-master compatibility check. The change is recorded as one Undo step. Existing nodes and shape metadata stay; new nodes are sharp. Both handle positions coincide with the selected point, so the added segment has no area. Independent behaviour-only rewrite after Fernando Díaz, Reset Type Studio, https://github.com/Reset-Type-Studio/Glyphs-Scripts, Apache-2.0 declared in README.md (no separate LICENSE file). Sources: Paths/Node Duplicator (all masters).py, Paths/Node Duplicator (current layer).py, and Paths/Node Duplicator + 2 Handles (all masters).py. No source code copied.

text: Promote straight segments where corresponding masters contain cubics. What: Promote straight segments where corresponding masters contain cubics. How: Compare each contour and segment with every declared master. Keep glyphs with mismatched contour counts, open paths or quadratic outlines. Endpoints stay. Why: Repair line-versus-cubic interpolation mismatches without moving endpoints. Use: Align starts and directions first (run Superaligner), then select glyphs, choose All masters, inspect the conversion rows, and Apply. Benefit: Repairs segment types across masters rather than merely reporting them. The non-modal panel previews the selected glyphs and chosen masters. A glyph with shared, scaled or rotated outline shapes is kept as a whole. Automatic-layer owners are kept. Bases of automatic composites are kept unless the shared consent option is enabled. Each Apply is recorded as one Undo step through the App history writer. Reload after changing the selection. Independent behaviour rewrite after Simon Cozens, GlyphsScripts/Make Compatible.py, MIT, copyright 2017 Simon Cozens. Repository: https://github.com/simoncozens/GlyphsScripts . No source code was copied.

text: Show every master of a glyph side by side with numbered contours, start points and directions. What it does: Each contour carries its index at the start node, a dot on the start node and an arrow along its first segment, so start-point and order mismatches between masters are visible at a glance before interpolation surprises you. Read-only: nothing in the font changes. How it works: Use the shared contour-order view to draw each master and label contour indices, start nodes and first-segment directions at their native positions. Why this design: A structural count cannot reveal a different start point or contour order; the drawing exposes those differences directly. How to use: Select a glyph and run Contours > Contour Order View. Compare matching contour numbers and direction arrows between the master panels before editing compatibility. Benefit: Review contour order and starts without reversing paths or changing interpolation structure.

text: Contours and nodes per glyph and master in one table, with incompatible glyphs flagged. What it does: Each cell reads "contours / nodes" for a master; a glyph is flagged when its masters differ, which breaks interpolation. Work on the selection or the whole font, then select the flagged glyphs in the Font window with one click. Read-only: nothing in the font changes. How it works: Read contour and node counts on the selection or whole font, grouped by master. Flag differing counts and keep the source snapshot for the selection action. Why this design: Count differences can rule out compatibility, but matching counts alone do not prove matching contour structure. How to use: Run Contours > Node Statistics. Choose the source scope, inspect each contours/nodes cell and use the action button to select flagged glyphs in the Font window. Benefit: Find count mismatches quickly while preserving node positions, topology and layer data.

text: Add on-curve nodes at the horizontal and vertical extremes of curves. What: For each selected glyph and master, the table lists every contour whose curves have an extreme without a node: the node count now and the number of extremes to add. Add Extremes inserts them. How: For each cubic curve, the script solves the derivative of x and of y for t; extremes closer than 2 % of the parameter t to an end node are ignored. FontLab's own split, flContour.insertNodeTo, inserts each node, so the curve keeps its shape up to FontLab's rounding of the new node. Cuts within 0.1 Manhattan units of an end or an earlier cut are not offered. The splits run from the last curve back, so the segment numbers of the earlier curves stay valid. TrueType (quadratic) contours and open contours are left alone. Why: Fonts need nodes at extremes for good hinting and rasterisation, and font tests flag missing extremes. With "Keep masters compatible" ticked, a glyph is held back when the masters would get different nodes, or when only some masters are in scope: different nodes break interpolation. Use: Select glyphs. Run the script. Choose the masters. Press Add Extremes. Press Reload selection after you change the selection. Benefit: Fixes many glyphs over many masters in one Undo step, and keeps the masters compatible. Safety: These shapes are listed and kept: shared outline data (an edit would change other glyphs too); shapes with scale, slant or rotation (an extreme in stored coordinates is not an extreme on screen). A glyph that has an automatic layer is listed and skipped. So is a glyph that is a base of an automatic composite, also through other composites, unless you tick "Also edit bases of automatic composites" (FontLab then rebuilds those composites; anchor recovery through Undo is not assured). The script keeps the compatibility check; writes disclose queued ids and possible date changes. After the write, it reads the node counts back. If FontLab fails part-way, the error says that native changes may remain. The change is recorded as one Undo step. The one-step write, the automatic-layer rule, the pending-update check and the panel are shared (fly.ap.contours.writer, fly.ap.contours.panel.model); the planner belongs to this script. Source: the author's own FontLab sample outlines_add_extremes.py, Apache-2.0. Adapted for the current FontLab 9 API.

text: Align selected geometry or space selected nodes at equal intervals. What: Six alignment choices and horizontal or vertical node distribution share one non-modal panel. Whole selected contours move as units. Partial contours contribute selected nodes. Components move by their transform; their base glyphs stay. Anchors are never moved: this tool cannot read anchor selection. Use Contour > Align Points to align selected anchors. How: Work in upright glyph coordinates; italic angle is not applied. Alignment uses the minimum, maximum or midpoint, or an explicit coordinate. Bounds include selected control points, so results can differ from Contour > Align Points. Component bounds use the transformed local bounding rectangle. Distribution sorts selected nodes on the chosen axis, keeps both endpoints, and divides their span equally. Ties keep contour/node order. Unselected adjacent handles follow their moved on-curve node by the same offset. Selected handles use their own targets. Node types and connection flags stay. Why: Contour > Align Points aligns points on the current layer. Element > Align / Distribute Shapes operates on shapes. This tool adds node distribution, several glyph layers or masters in one Undo step, and a numeric preview. Use: Select nodes or components in a Glyph window. Choose an operation, inspect the table and Apply. All nodes is for alignment only; distribution requires selected nodes. All masters processes each loaded glyph's masters; node selection is read separately in each layer. Reload selection after choosing other glyphs or editor layers. Apply reads selected layers and geometry again. A single item with Selection bounds has no move. Choose Coordinate to move it. Two selected nodes that share one curve handle are kept; select the handle too, or align them one at a time. Automatic guide/metric snapping and italic deskew are not provided. Benefit: Repeat alignment without reopening a dialog. Each Apply is recorded as one Undo step. Automatic-layer glyphs and their bases are skipped. Locked layers/shapes, shared node data and contours with their own transform are kept and named in the preview; the other eligible items can still change. Advances, anchors and guides stay. FontLab can round coordinates to its grid. Source: Independent behaviour-only rewrite after Alex Slobzheninov, https://github.com/slobzheninov/Glyphs-Scripts, Align/Align Top.py, Align Bottom.py, Align Left.py, Align Right.py, Align Horizontal Center.py, Align Vertical Center.py, Distribute Nodes Horizontally.py and Distribute Nodes Vertically.py, Apache-2.0. The sources credit Rainer Erich Scheichelbauer (mekkablue, Apache-2.0). No source code, identifiers or comments were copied.

text: Set the contour direction of the selected glyphs: outer and inner contours. What: For each selected glyph and master, the table lists every closed contour that runs the wrong way, with its current direction. Correct reverses them. How: Native flContour.clockwise gives the direction; contains tests all segment start and mid points, as FontLab's own direction command does. Nesting within the same shape decides each edit. If layer-wide nesting would give a different answer, the contour is listed as "inside another shape, direction left" and kept. Overlapping outer contours stay outer. Native segments include TrueType implied on-curve points. PostScript outer contours run counter-clockwise; TrueType uses the opposite convention. Native flContour.reverse reverses in place. Why: The result depends only on the shape, not on how the font was drawn, so imports and pasted outlines get the right direction. A wrong direction makes holes fill in some renderers and spoils overlap removal. Use: Select glyphs. Run the script. Choose the masters. Press Correct. Press Reload selection after you change the selection. Benefit: Fixes many glyphs over many masters in one Undo step, and lists each wrong contour before anything changes. Safety: Open contours have no direction and are not counted. These shapes are listed and kept, but count for the cross-shape safety check: shared outline data (an edit would change other glyphs too); shapes with scale, slant or rotation (a mirror in the transform turns the visible direction round). After writing, a status note reports a newly introduced final off-curve with raw Smooth (fl#8517), which FontLab may change on save. Existing conditions are not reported as new. Check node types after VFJ reopen. A reversal renumbers the nodes of that contour. The panel opens with All masters chosen. When only one master has a wrong contour, check master compatibility after the change: the other masters keep their node order. A glyph that has an automatic layer is listed and skipped. So is a glyph that is a base of an automatic composite, also through other composites, unless you tick "Also edit bases of automatic composites" (FontLab then rebuilds those composites; anchor recovery through Undo is not assured). The script keeps the compatibility check; writes disclose queued ids and possible date changes. After the write, it reads every direction back. If FontLab fails part-way, the error says that native changes may remain. The change is recorded as one Undo step. The one-step write, the automatic-layer rule, the pending-update check and the panel are shared (fly.ap.contours.writer, fly.ap.contours.panel.model); the planner belongs to this script. Source: the author's own FontLab sample outlines_correct_direction.py, Apache-2.0. Adapted for the current FontLab 9 API.

Each Apply is recorded as one Undo step through the App history writer. Reload after changing the selection. text: Find contours drawn twice in the same layer and keep only the first copy. What: For each selected glyph and master, the table lists every contour that repeats an earlier contour of the same layer. Delete removes the copies. How: Two contours are duplicates when they have the same nodes in the same cyclic order, from any start node in the same direction, and each node pair lies within the tolerance (in glyph coordinates, so moved shapes compare where you see them). On-curve and off-curve nodes must match. The first contour of a group stays; FontLab's own flShape.removeContour removes the others. Reversed duplicate groups are listed as "reversed duplicate, kept". Every member stays, including further copies: their winding can cancel. Open contours are kept; cyclic rotation changes their open endpoints. Why: Same-direction duplicates are invisible in a filled preview, but they break overlap removal, double the ink in some renderers and confuse contour order tools. With "Keep masters compatible" ticked, a glyph is held back when the masters would lose different contours, or when only some masters are in scope. Use: Select glyphs. Run the script. Set the tolerance and the masters. Press Delete. Press Reload selection after you change the selection. Benefit: Removes hidden copies over many glyphs and masters in one Undo step, and names the contour each copy repeats. Safety: These shapes are listed and kept: shared outline data (an edit would change other glyphs too); shapes with scale, slant or rotation (stored nodes are not visible nodes). A glyph that has an automatic layer is listed and skipped. So is a glyph that is a base of an automatic composite, also through other composites, unless you tick "Also edit bases of automatic composites" (FontLab then rebuilds those composites; anchor recovery through Undo is not assured). The script keeps the compatibility check; writes disclose queued ids and possible date changes. After the write, it reads the contour counts back. If FontLab fails part-way, the error says that native changes may remain. The change is recorded as one Undo step. The one-step write, the automatic-layer rule, the pending-update check and the panel are shared (fly.ap.contours.writer, fly.ap.contours.panel.model); the planner belongs to this script. Source: the author's own FontLab sample outlines_delete_duplicate_contours.py, Apache-2.0. Adapted for the current FontLab 9 API.

text: Delete contours whose area is below a threshold: specks from drawing or tracing. What: For each selected glyph and master, the table lists every contour smaller than the threshold, with its area and position. Delete removes them. How: The area is the exact area of the curves in square font units, measured by fly.ap.contours.selection.model.unsigned_area (FontTools' area pen). Open contours are listed as "open contour, kept" and are never deleted. A contour counts as small when its area is strictly below the threshold. This is the same rule as Contours > Select Small Contours, so you can select first and look, then delete with the same number. FontLab's own flShape.removeContour removes each contour. Why: Specks are hard to see in a filled preview but end up in the font. With "Keep masters compatible" ticked, a glyph is held back when the masters would lose different contours, or when only some masters are in scope: different contour counts break interpolation. text: Find curve handles that sit on their own node, and clean them up. What: For each selected glyph and master, the table lists every contour with retracted handles: curves whose two handles both sit on their nodes, and curves with one such handle. Fix turns the first kind into lines and, when you ask for it, pulls single handles out. How: A handle counts as retracted when it is closer than half a unit to its own node. A curve with two retracted handles is a straight line in disguise: FontLab's own flNode.convertToLine, called on the end node, removes the handles and resets the smooth flags. With "Pull single handles out to ⅓", a lone retracted handle moves a third of the way towards the other handle: the curve then has a real tangent at that node, but its shape changes slightly. TrueType (quadratic) contours are left alone. Why: Retracted handles give a zero tangent: hinting, offsetting, stroke expansion and some rasterisers handle them badly. With "Keep masters compatible" ticked, a glyph is held back when the masters would get different curves, or when only some masters are in scope. Use: Select glyphs. Run the script. Choose the option and the masters. Press Fix. Press Reload selection after you change the selection. Benefit: Finds and fixes a common outline fault over many glyphs and masters in one Undo step. Safety: Pulling a single handle on a Smooth base can leave the handles non-collinear. FontLab may later align them again. Converting a curve to a line recomputes the smooth flags at both ends. These shapes are listed and kept: shared outline data (an edit would change other glyphs too); shapes with scale, slant or rotation (stored distances are not visible distances). A pulled handle lands on a whole unit, a third of the way to the other handle, so FontLab's rounding preference cannot move it again. A glyph that has an automatic layer is listed and skipped. So is a glyph that is a base of an automatic composite, also through other composites, unless you tick "Also edit bases of automatic composites" (FontLab then rebuilds those composites; anchor recovery through Undo is not assured). The script keeps the compatibility check; writes disclose queued ids and possible date changes. After the write, it reads node counts and handle positions back. If FontLab fails part-way, the error says that native changes may remain. The change is recorded as one Undo step. text: Move the start node of every closed contour to its bottom-left on-curve node. What: For each selected glyph and master, the table lists every contour whose start node moves, and the node that becomes the start. Optimize applies the moves. How: The bottom-left node is the lowest on-curve node; on a tie, the leftmost one. "Match current master" finds it in the current master and uses the same node number in every other master whose contour has the same node count, so the masters stay compatible. "Bottom-left in each master" finds it in each master on its own. FontLab's own flContour.setStartPoint turns the node list round in place; this is meant to keep the node flags. See Safety for VFJ reopen. Why: A predictable start node makes masters easier to compare, helps interpolation and keeps the order of points in exported fonts stable. Use: Select glyphs. Run the script. Choose the rule and the masters. Press Optimize. Press Reload selection after you change the selection. Benefit: Sets consistent start points over many glyphs and masters in one Undo step. Safety: A status note reports only a newly introduced final off-curve with raw Smooth (fl#8517), which FontLab may change on save. Check node types after VFJ reopen. Open contours keep their start. These shapes are listed and kept: shared outline data (an edit would change other glyphs too); shapes with scale, slant or rotation (bottom-left in stored coordinates is not bottom-left on screen). A new start renumbers the nodes, so the panel opens with All masters chosen. With "Keep masters compatible" ticked, a glyph is kept when its masters would get different start nodes, or when other masters need the move too but are not chosen. A glyph that has an automatic layer is listed and skipped. So is a glyph that is a base of an automatic composite, also through other composites, unless you tick "Also edit bases of automatic composites" (FontLab then rebuilds those composites; anchor recovery through Undo is not assured). The script keeps the compatibility check; writes disclose queued ids and possible date changes. Every move is planned before the first one is written, so the current master stays a valid reference. After the write, the script reads the start nodes back. If FontLab fails part-way, the error says that native changes may remain. The change is recorded as one Undo step. The one-step write, the automatic-layer rule, the pending-update check and the panel are shared (fly.ap.contours.writer, fly.ap.contours.panel.model); the planner belongs to this script. text: Remove overlaps in the outline shapes of the selected glyphs. What: For each selected glyph and master, the table lists every outline shape whose contours overlap: the contour count now and after the merge. Remove Overlap merges them. Shapes without overlap stay untouched. Overlaps between separate shapes are not merged. This tool tests intersections between contours; a single self-intersecting contour is kept. How: Each shape goes through FontLab's FontGate engine: a copy is made with flShape.convertToFgShape, fgShape.removeOverlap merges it (a shape has an overlap when native contours intersect or same-direction contours nest), and flShape.assign writes the result back into the same shape object. The start node of each new contour moves back to an old start point when one survives the merge, as FontLab's own command does. The preview runs the same merge on a copy, so the numbers are exact. Why: Overlapping contours print and render fine in many places, but fonts for the web, variable fonts and many tools need clean outlines. With "Keep masters compatible" ticked, a glyph is held back when the masters would get different contours, or when only some masters are in scope: the merge would break interpolation. Use: Select glyphs. Run the script. Choose the masters. Press Remove Overlap. Press Reload selection after you change the selection. Benefit: Cleans many glyphs over many masters in one Undo step, and lists each merge before anything changes. Safety: A status note reports only a newly introduced final off-curve with raw Smooth (fl#8517), which FontLab may change on save. Check node types after VFJ reopen. The merge rebuilds the contours of a merged shape: node names, node flags, contour names and corner_smooth (fl#8569) in that shape are not kept. FontGate assign also replaces the shape appearance. No name, note or appearance preservation is claimed for that round trip. These shapes are listed and kept: shared outline data (an edit would change other glyphs too); shapes with a transform (FontGate would merge them in stored coordinates); shapes with an open contour (an open contour has no inside). A glyph that has an automatic layer is listed and skipped. So is a glyph that is a base of an automatic composite, also through other composites, unless you tick "Also edit bases of automatic composites" (FontLab then rebuilds those composites; anchor recovery through Undo is not assured). The script keeps the compatibility check; writes disclose queued ids and possible date changes. After the write, it reads the contour counts back. If FontLab fails part-way, the error says that native changes may remain. The change is recorded as one Undo step. The one-step write, the automatic-layer rule, the pending-update check and the panel are shared (fly.ap.contours.writer, fly.ap.contours.panel.model); the planner belongs to this script. text: Slant the selected glyphs by an angle, optionally the font's italic angle. If FontLab fails part-way, the error says that native changes may remain. The change is recorded as one Undo step. The one-step write, the automatic-layer rule, the pending-update check and the panel are shared (fly.ap.contours.writer, fly.ap.contours.panel.model); the planner belongs to this script. text: Scale, skew, rotate and move the outlines of the selected glyphs, with a preview. What: Set scale (x and y, in %), skew and rotation (in degrees) and a move (in units), and pick the origin. The preview paints the first selected glyph of the current master before (faint) and after (accent). The table lists each glyph and master with its node count and origin. Transform applies it. How: The script builds one affine matrix: move the origin to 0, 0; scale; skew; rotate; move back; then move by the offset. The origin is computed per layer: bounding box centre or bottom-left, the glyph origin, or the advance centre on the baseline. Each shape gets the matrix the way FontLab's own layer transform does: a plain own outline gets new node positions (FontLab may round them); a component, a shared outline or a scaled shape keeps its nodes and gets the composed transform. Anchors follow when you tick "Move anchors too". The advance width and the guides stay. Why: One panel does what otherwise takes several steps, for many glyphs and masters at once, and shows the result first. For a slant about the x-height with the font's italic angle, use Contours > Slant. Use: Select glyphs. Run the script. Set the values, the origin and the masters. Press Transform. Press Reload selection after you change the selection. Benefit: Exact, repeatable transforms over many glyphs and masters in one Undo step. Safety: These cases block or limit the edit: an anchor that would move onto 0, 0 blocks Apply: FontLab cannot redo that move (fl#8527); a glyph that has an automatic layer is listed and skipped. So is a glyph that is a base of an automatic composite, also through other composites, unless you tick "Also edit bases of automatic composites" (FontLab then rebuilds those composites; anchor recovery through Undo is not assured). The script discloses queued ids and their possible date changes. After the write, it reads transforms, a node per baked shape and the anchors back. If FontLab fails part-way, the error says that native changes may remain. The change is recorded as one Undo step. The one-step write, the automatic-layer rule, the pending-update check, the preview and the panel are shared (fontlabapp.contours.writer, fontlabapp.contours.transform.model); the matrix math is fontlabapp.contours.affine; the planner belongs to this script. Source: the author's own FontLab sample outlines_transform_dialog.py, Apache-2.0. Adapted for the current FontLab 9 API.
